statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail is 8% in the low band roughly two and a half hours into the Sunday Globex session.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. A narrow evidence-based danger window is flagged over the 13:00-15:00 UTC window containing Monday's US cash open, where an opening-auction imbalance can extend before it retraces. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ extends to a 30,063.50 session high and holds 30,042.00 (+0.42%) after a two-way reopen; Tail edges to 8% while a 5.00% 10-year and $99 WTI hold Stress at 35%
body:
About two and a half hours into the Globex session the NQ price path is higher but shallow. Futures print 30,042.00, up 124.75 points (+0.42%) against the 29,917.25 Friday settle, inside an observed 29,904.50-30,063.50 range, and Investing.com's delayed feed corroborates at 30,039.50 (+0.41%). The structurally important detail is unchanged from the prior hour: the session low was set below the settle before the recovery, so discovery has been genuinely two-way, and the entire excursion spans just 0.53%. The index is now holding near its session high, which is a single Tail amplifier, but on a thin Sunday book with a sub-1% range it is not the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail measure is defined against.

The cash reference is Friday's NDX close at 29,644.17, up 0.67%, in a mixed tape: the S&P 500 added 0.17% to 7,650.50 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.39% while the Dow shed 0.18%. Internals were split rather than aligned - Broadcom rose about 3% and Micron about 3.9% while Meta fell 2.4% and Oracle 2% - and the Finviz latest-session context is consistent with that, showing megacaps evenly divided four to four and Technology up 0.84% against Communication Services down 0.74%. Split internals argue for rotation and dispersion, not index-level one-way structure. Note that this breadth context is delayed, latest-session data and is not evidence of live price path.

The macro backdrop is what holds Stress elevated. The FOMC raised rates 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September, its first hike in three years, and signalled more tightening; Kashkari said on Sunday that inflation is still too high in all aspects of the economy, with Fed officials estimating August core inflation near 3.6%. The 10-year rebounded about 7 basis points to 4.997% on Friday, a level last seen in 2007, against a 2-year at 4.67% on the latest H.15 observation. Crude remains historically high at $99.27 WTI and $103.06 Brent, but it has fallen for three straight sessions as Saudi flows through the Strait of Hormuz recovered toward 2.8 million barrels per day and US Central Command reported the highest Hormuz oil and LNG throughput in six months. VIX closed at 14.81, down 4.08%, which is a calm volatility reading against that backdrop.

The live catalyst set for the week is diplomatic rather than macro. US and Chinese officials are meeting in New York ahead of a presidential summit expected to cover trade, artificial intelligence and the Middle East, and President Trump has indicated he would probably be open to meeting Iranian President Pezeshkian at the UN General Assembly. That combination is the plausible source of headline-driven whipsaw this week, but under the evidence standard applied here an unresolved diplomatic process raises Stress and widens dispersion rather than establishing the Tail path in advance.

Net: Tail 8%, up one point on the session-high hold and the modest extension, which keeps the mapped state at EA_ON and green. Stress rises to 35% as the 10-year is confirmed at 5.00% rather than the 4.94% H.15 print used earlier, partly offset by the easing energy impulse. Confidence is 76% on two corroborating live futures feeds, verified yield, oil and volatility levels, a verified seven-day calendar and verified weekend reporting, discounted for the absence of live cash-market cross-asset confirmation over the weekend.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available and describe an unbroken low-Tail regime across the Sunday of the weekend halt and into the Globex reopen. Tail held between 4% and 7% in every hour, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout, and rose only in the final two hours as the reopen produced its first live price path. Stress drifted from 25% early on 20 September into a 30-34% band as the post-hike rate backdrop and the elevated oil complex accumulated, peaking at 34% in the two hours after the reopen. Confidence ranged from 70% to 76%, dipping in the deepest part of the halt when no live price path existed and recovering once futures reopened. Dominant mode was normal in all 24 hours. The present assessment continues that sequence with Tail at 8%.
outlookSummary: The cycle covers the remainder of the Asian session, the European session, the Monday US cash session through the 20:00 UTC close, the CME maintenance halt and the Tuesday Globex reopen. Tail is projected to stay inside the low band in all 24 hours, so the mapped policy state remains EA_ON throughout. The projected peak is 12% in the hour containing the 13:30 UTC US cash open, followed by 11% in the hour after it, which is why the flagged danger window spans 13:00-15:00 UTC; a secondary 10% is projected for the 10:30 UTC Fed Goolsbee speech, the 12:30 UTC Chicago Fed release, the 15:30 UTC bill auctions and the closing hour into 20:00 UTC. The cycle low of 6% falls in the 21:00-22:00 UTC maintenance halt, when no NQ price path exists. Stress is projected between 33% and 38%, held up by a 5.00% 10-year, roughly $100 crude and a Fed that has just resumed hiking, and capped by the three-session decline in oil as Hormuz throughput recovers. Confidence decays from 76% to 68% across the cycle as the evidence base ages. These are conditional projections: no future price-path structure is treated as already observed, and an upgrade would require observed shallow pullbacks with repeated extension after failed retracements.
